nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November
22nd.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 210642
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
142 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Very mild with near record highs in the mid to upper 60s
  today.

- 60-80% chance of rain Sunday afternoon. Scattered light 
  showers likely at times with rainfall amounts up to 0.10".

- Seasonable next week with highs in the upper 30s to low 40s.

- Thanksgiving forecast: highs near 40 degrees with 20-30%
  chances for scattered rain and snow showers.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 141 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

Friday was absolutely pleasant for late November with highs well 
into the 60s. We'll play this track again today with a 576dm ridge 
still in place. These heights are a touch lower that 24 hours prior 
while 850mb temps are about 2C warmer and our morning lows are 
warmer as well, providing a better spring board for the 
afternoon. This all to say afternoon highs will be comparable to
Friday, once again challenging records.

Back to reality next week in the wake of a cold front that moves 
through later Sunday. Breezy and mild ahead of the front Sunday 
morning with rain arriving to northwest Indiana during the early 
afternoon, gradually tracking east thereafter. Rain amounts 
will be light, at less than 0.10", as the best upper-level 
forcing lifts north and the precipitation shield along the front
battles preexisting high pressure over the Appalachians.

Canadian high pressure spills over the Northern Plains Sunday 
night through Monday with a secondary shortwave noted Monday 
night. This shortwave still threatens to provide a brief period 
of lake effect to the eastern Great Lakes but duration, if at 
all, appears brief. High pressure quickly arriving limits fetch
and equilibrium levels, as guidance continues to offer a 
variety of coverage solutions for any POPs. The official forecast
remains dry at this time.

An eastern US trough near Thanksgiving remains somewhat murky 
locally, yet most signs favor any precipitation to be east of the 
IWX coverage area. Using Grand Ensemble clusters, a GEFS/ENS/GEPS 
split yields only a 35% chance of precipitation >0.01", while a 4th 
cluster weighted toward the GEFS yields a 40% chance. 20-30% POPs 
remain the forecast, primarily along and east of I-69 corridor. 

Broad upper-level troughing remains in place through the end of the 
week. An upstream ridge is noted thereafter which may promote a
moderating trend once more as the calendar turns to December. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 1222 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

With surface high pressure to the east and a trough to our west, the 
area is securely in a warm advection pattern. The theta-e plume of 
warmth and moisture won't make it into the area this period so VFR 
conditions are expected to continue for one more day as dry air 
continues to rule out. Turning to winds, they continue to remain out 
of the south through the period and the diurnal peak allows for 
mixing, but mixing heights stay relatively low keeping gusts to 
minimal through the period. Some sustained winds around 10 kts are 
still possible.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Air Quality Alert from 6 PM this evening to 10 AM EST Sunday 
     for INZ005.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

spc.summary: Isolated strong to severe storms are possible from western Oklahoma into south-central Kansas on Saturday.
spc.text:
SPC AC 210540

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1140 PM CST Fri Nov 20 2026

   Valid 211200Z - 221200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM WESTERN OK
   INTO SOUTH-CENTRAL KS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe storms are possible from western Oklahoma
   into south-central Kansas on Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Shortwave trough currently progressing through central CA is
   forecast to continue quickly eastward across the Southwest early
   Saturday, reaching the southern High Plains by the late afternoon.
   The wave is expected to continue eastward Saturday night through
   Sunday morning, ending the period extending from western IA through
   central OK. 

   At the surface, the low currently over southeast CO is forecast to
   slowly shift eastward/southeastward throughout much of the day while
   gradually deepening. After 00Z, this low is forecast to eject
   quickly northeastward as a southeastward-progressing cold front
   surges through the central Plains, TX Panhandle, and much of OK. By
   12Z, this cold front will likely extend from the surface low (now in
   the northern MO/IL border vicinity) southwestward to another weak
   low over southeast OK. Showers and thunderstorms are anticipated
   along and ahead of this front, with the highest thunderstorm
   coverage expected from northern OK in central/eastern KS.

   Isolated thunderstorms are also possible across the Pacific
   Northwest coast, where persistent forcing for ascent and cold
   mid-level temperatures could support a few lightning flashes.
   Isolated thunderstorms are also possible from the FL Peninsula to
   the Carolina Coast. Here, ample low-level moisture will combine with
   ascent attendant to a weak mid-level cyclone to support isolated to
   widely scattered thunderstorms.

   ...Central/Southern Plains...
   Warm-air advection showers and isolated thunderstorms will precede
   the cold front during the afternoon beginning in northwest TX and
   the eastern TX Panhandle before expanding northeastward across
   western/central OK into central/eastern KS. Strong southerly
   low-level flow is expected throughout the day and dewpoints will
   likely be in the mid 50s. This moisture should support some elevated
   buoyancy, but cool surface temperatures will limit surface-based
   buoyancy. In general, limited buoyancy should temper the severe
   potential with these storms.

   Additional thunderstorms are expected along the cold front Saturday
   evening and overnight. Continued low-level moisture advection will
   likely bring dewpoints into the upper 50s, but temperatures will
   remain relatively cool (i.e. in the upper 50s/low 60s), with
   surface-based convective inhibition persisting. Even so, cooling
   mid-level temperatures could still result in modest buoyancy from
   western OK into south-central KS. Strong speed shear will also be in
   place, with the resulting combination of buoyancy and shear
   supporting the potential for a few storms capable of hail.
   Additionally, despite persisting low-level stability, a few strong
   gusts could still reach the surface with any bowing segments along
   the front.

   ...Coastal Carolinas...
   Most guidance takes a weak surface low across the northern FL
   Peninsula during the day Saturday while it gradually occludes. This
   evolution largely keeps the higher dewpoints and greater buoyancy
   offshore, with an associated limiting of the severe potential. If
   the moist sector does advect inland, strong low-level wind fields
   support the potential for a couple of shallow rotating storms across
   parts of the coastal Carolinas, and sporadic damaging gusts or a
   brief tornado would be possible. However, given the expectation that
   the moist sector will remain offshore, the potential for severe
   thunderstorms is very low.

   ..Mosier/Squitieri.. 11/21/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 210700

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0100 AM CST Sat Nov 21 2026

   Valid 221200Z - 231200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   SOUTH TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered thunderstorms are possible over parts of the middle and
   lower Mississippi Valley and into South Texas Sunday. Isolated
   severe storms are possible.

   ...Mid/Lower MS Valley...
   An upper trough over the southern and central Plains is forecast to
   move eastward and weaken through Sunday. A weak surface low and cold
   front, attendant to the trough, will move from OK/TX toward southern
   AR, northern LA and western MS by Sunday evening. Ahead of the
   front, southerly winds should allow for upper 50s to low 60s F
   surface dewpoints to reach as far north as central AR. This, along
   with diurnal heating should support modest buoyancy sufficient for
   thunderstorms.

   Remnant thunderstorms will likely be ongoing ahead of the front from
   southern IL/MO into eastern OK/TX. While buoyancy should remain
   overall modest (MUCAPE ~500 J/kg) these storms and additional
   development may gradually strengthen through the afternoon. Flow
   aloft will not be overly strong as the upper wave weakens and lifts
   away to the northeast, but 25-35 kt of deep-layer shear will remain
   marginally supportive of a transient stronger storm or two. Damaging
   gusts, and hail would be possible, though confidence in this
   scenario is low. Convection should weaken as the cold front
   continues eastward into a more stable airmass Sunday evening.

   ...South Texas...
   Mid to upper 60s F surface dewpoints will be in place ahead of the
   cold front across South TX and toward the middle TX Coast. Though
   forcing aloft will be rather weak with the primary shortwave trough
   displaced to the north, a belt of enhanced mid-level winds within a
   weak subtropical jet will exist across the region. Convergence along
   the approaching front may be sufficient to initiate thunderstorms
   during the afternoon given weak to moderate buoyancy (max MUCAPE
   1000-1500 J/kg). Isolated stronger clusters or transient supercells
   may be possible, though storms may have a tendency to be undercut by
   the advancing front. The mid-level lapse rates are forecast to be
   rather modest but, a sporadic damaging gust or isolated hail could
   occur. Convection should begin to weaken as it moves offshore Sunday
   evening.

   ..Lyons.. 11/21/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 210817

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0217 AM CST Sat Nov 21 2026

   Valid 231200Z - 241200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   The shortwave trough over the Mid MS Valley will merge with a
   deepening upper trough over the eastern Great Lakes and Northeast
   Monday. Shortwave ridging will intensify behind the departing wave
   over the central US ahead of a second weaker trough moving over the
   southern Rockies. At the surface, the cold front will continue
   southeastward and offshore into the Gulf. Strong high pressure will
   develop behind it, reinforcing an offshore pressure gradient. 
   Sufficient onshore moisture and buoyancy will be limited to the
   immediate northern Gulf Coast Monday afternoon. Isolated
   thunderstorms are possible, but buoyancy will be scant, precluding
   severe potential.

   ..Lyons.. 11/21/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
